football_evidence.assessment: Most of the 3.5-point difference traces to last season’s share of the rating (about 2.5 points), which the closing market has historically priced differently. That explains the gap; it does not make either number a bet.

contradicting: When Purdue has the ball (the red zone): Purdue’s offense succeeds on 36.2% of its red-zone plays, and Washington’s defense allows success on 39.0% of opponent red-zone plays (FBS average 43.8%).
